scenes.say: This man's scam was so famous, it's still named after him.
scenes.cap: This man's scam was so FAMOUS, it's still NAMED after him.

scenes.say: Boston, nineteen twenty. Charles Ponzi made a promise. Fifty percent profit, in forty-five days.
scenes.cap: Boston, 1920. Charles Ponzi made a promise. 50% PROFIT, in 45 DAYS.

scenes.say: His secret? Postal reply coupons. Buy them cheap in Europe, and swap them in America for more.
scenes.cap: His secret? POSTAL REPLY COUPONS. Buy them cheap in Europe, and swap them in America for MORE.

scenes.say: It sounded smart. So people lined up down the street with their savings.
scenes.cap: It sounded SMART. So people lined up down the street with their SAVINGS.

scenes.say: Money flooded in. He bought a mansion, and even took control of a bank.
scenes.cap: Money FLOODED in. He bought a MANSION, and even took control of a BANK.

scenes.say: But here's the trick. He wasn't really buying coupons. He paid old investors with new investors' money.
scenes.cap: But here's the trick. He wasn't really buying coupons. He paid OLD investors with NEW investors' money.

scenes.say: Then a journalist did the math. To cover it all, Ponzi would need a hundred and sixty million coupons.
scenes.cap: Then a journalist did the MATH. To cover it all, Ponzi would need 160 MILLION coupons.

scenes.say: There were only about twenty-seven thousand in circulation.
scenes.cap: There were only about 27,000 in circulation.

scenes.say: In August nineteen twenty, it all collapsed. Investors lost about twenty million dollars.
scenes.cap: In August 1920, it all COLLAPSED. Investors lost about $20 MILLION.

scenes.say: Ponzi went to prison, was deported to Italy, and died poor in Brazil.
scenes.cap: Ponzi went to PRISON, was DEPORTED to Italy, and died POOR in Brazil.

scenes.say: Today, every scam that pays old investors with new money carries his name.
scenes.cap: Today, every scam that pays old investors with new money carries his NAME.

scenes.say: Follow Paper Trail, for the money stories nobody tells you.
scenes.cap: Follow PAPER TRAIL for the money stories nobody tells you.

upload.description:
In 1920, Charles Ponzi promised 50% profit in 45 days using international postal reply coupons. In reality, he paid old investors with new investors' money. When a journalist did the math, it all collapsed - investors lost about $20 million.

Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ponzi
